VIKRAMSOLR.why: Down more than half from the ₹332 issue price. The trigger in August 2026 was Q1 FY27: profit fell 85% to ₹20 crore even though revenue rose 38% to ₹1,563 crore, because EBITDA margin collapsed to 8% from 21% as raw material costs rose 63%. Module prices outside the domestic-content category keep falling and cells remain in oversupply, per JM Financial.
VIKRAMSOLR.outlook: UBS is Neutral (₹215 target) and JM Financial Add (₹219). JM says the key watch item is commissioning its cell plant and getting efficiency stable. The sector-wide weakness (Waaree also disappointed) means margin recovery is unproven.

URBANCO.why: Fast growth: FY26 total income rose 34% to ₹1,692 crore and Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore with completed orders up 79% to 13.2 million; shares jumped about 13-18% after Q1 despite a ₹92 crore loss. The core India consumer service business made ₹131 crore adjusted EBITDA in FY26. After a low near ₹96 in March 2026, SBI Mutual Fund bought about 4% (about ₹632 crore). Losses come from the InstaHelp housekeeping launch and Native appliances.
URBANCO.outlook: InstaHelp passed 100,000 daily orders on 2 August 2026; excluding it, Q1 adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to ₹67 crore. Profit depends on InstaHelp and new products reaching break-even. One consensus target was about ₹133 and the stock looks richly valued. FY26 net loss was ₹235 crore (against a profit last year).

IVALUE.why: Weaker results: December 2025 quarter profit fell 17% to ₹15.7 crore on sales down 9.6%, and a source reports a further sharp quarterly decline in Q1 FY27. Foreign holding fell from 4.9% to 2.2%. The cause of the price fall is mostly inferred from these results and a blog citing foreign selling and de-rating.
IVALUE.outlook: No broker targets or formal 2026 forecast were found. FY25 had been solid (revenue +20% to ₹916 crore, profit +15% to ₹83 crore). The FY26 annual report was filed in August 2026 but its contents were not found; the next quarters decide whether the decline reverses.

STYL.why: Fell about 47% in the six months to April 2026 (to near ₹228 from a high of ₹437), then recovered to around ₹400 by August. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% to ₹376 crore and profit 64% to ₹60.3 crore year on year, though profit was about 26% lower than the previous quarter. Demand tailwind: banks upgrading to secure and metal cards.
STYL.outlook: FY27 guidance was withheld citing macro uncertainty, to be revisited after Q1; capex of ₹160-200 crore is planned. Top-10 customers were 68.6% of revenue in Q1 FY26, so client concentration is a risk. No formal broker research was found.

SOLARWORLD.why: Down about 54% over a year. Q2 FY26 revenue fell 2.8% and profit fell 58% as a ₹6.7 crore loss in manufacturing hit EBITDA (down 48.6%). Sources also blame foreign selling and sector weakness, though foreign holding is only about 1.2%. The company is net-debt free.
SOLARWORLD.outlook: No formal company guidance or broker forecast was found. Listed risks: macro slowdown, input cost pressure, and competition in solar EPC and products. Its manufacturing arm needs to stop losing money to turn the trend.

PACEDIGITK.why: Slid after listing at ₹225: the stock fell after weak June 2025 quarter operations and again when Q2 FY26 profit dropped 33% on revenue down 37%. After Q1 FY27 it touched ₹186.2 on 6 August 2026. EBITDA margin was 15.5% against 21.8% a year ago, even though revenue rose 51% to ₹555 crore and profit 14% to ₹62.5 crore.
PACEDIGITK.outlook: Energy (battery storage, BESS) dominates: energy order book ₹8,453 crore and total about ₹10,803 crore, telecom order book ₹2,350 crore. One article reports guidance of ₹3,200-3,400 crore for FY27, not confirmed in filings. The outlook rests on executing the BESS business and recovering margins.

FABTECH.why: Below the issue price despite good numbers: Q4 FY26 profit rose 46% to ₹22 crore on a 17.5% sales rise to ₹158.5 crore, order book above ₹900 crore, and the shares jumped 8% on the day. The stock is still down about 20% over a year (52-week range ₹126-262). The cause of the fall was not stated; heavy upfront capex and modest returns (ROE about 13%, ROCE about 8%) are possible factors.
FABTECH.outlook: Management expects EBITDA margin to rise gradually to 9.9-10.5% in FY27 on operating leverage, and is exploring acquisitions in life sciences. It has front-loaded capex ahead of demand. No analyst targets were found.

LGEINDIA.why: Up about 52% since the October 2025 listing, hitting records in October 2026. Brokers credit premiumisation, calibrated price hikes (ACs +7-9%, and 5-6% from 1 October), and localisation: compressor production from Q3 FY27, AC manufacturing in Q4 FY27. Q4 FY26 was soft (adjusted EBITDA margin 11.7%, profit -8%).
LGEINDIA.outlook: Motilal Oswal is Buy with a ₹2,080 target and expects 14% revenue, 24% EBITDA and 25% profit CAGRs over FY26-29. Nuvama targets ₹1,990, Centrum ₹1,850; Nomura trimmed its target. Valuation is rich (P/E near 61), and June-quarter revenue and profit fell from March.

LENSKART.why: Store-led growth: 3,327 active stores in 16 countries, 603 net additions last year, same-store sales growth near 15%, revenue up to ₹9,002 crore from ₹6,803 crore. Q3 FY26 revenue rose 38% to ₹2,308 crore and the stock jumped over 12%; nine-month profit rose 285% to ₹297 crore. Profit is uneven: one report said Q4 profit dipped about 9% while revenue rose 46% (low-quality source).
LENSKART.outlook: Motilal Oswal initiated Buy at ₹600 and sees room for about 25% revenue CAGR, but also says valuation already reflects growth. Average rating Buy from seven analysts with a median target of ₹525 (LSEG). Risks: cash for store expansion and the Hyderabad manufacturing build.
